result.topic_en: Rough pencil notes on lacunary power series $\sum x^{a_n}$ with $a_n/n\to\infty$ or $a_{n+1}-a_n\to\infty$, with the example $a_n=n^2$, $\phi(n)=\sqrt{n}$, and a bound $O(\sqrt{n})$ for a sum of cosines $\cos 1^2 x+\dots+\cos n^2 x$.
result.transcription:
$\frac{a_n}{n} \longrightarrow \infty;$

$\Sigma\, x^{a_n}.$

$a_1\ a_2 \cdots$

$a_{n+1} - a_n \longrightarrow \infty$

$a_n = n^2$ $\qquad \phi(n) = \sqrt{n}$

$\cos 1^2 x + \cdots + \cos n^2 x = O\sqrt{n}$

methods.what: Lacunary power series with exponents growing faster than n
Gap condition: differences of consecutive exponents tend to infinity
Example of square exponents with comparison function sqrt(n)
Bound for the sum of cosines of square multiples (theta-type trigonometric sum)

items.english: The sum cos(1^2 x) + ... + cos(n^2 x) is O(sqrt n).
